11: # 除く (のぞく) — remove; exclude
12: 
13: ## Meaning
14: 
15: 除く means removing something or excluding it from a set. It is transitive: を marks what is removed or left out.
16: The polite form is 除きます (のぞきます); its て-form is 除いて (のぞいて).
17: 
18: - 野菜の種を除きます。 (やさいのたねをのぞきます。) — I remove the seeds from the vegetables.
19: - 日曜日を除いて、毎日開いています。 (にちようびをのぞいて、まいにちあいています。) — It is open every day except Sunday.
20: 
21: ## How the kanji combine
22: 
23: [除](../kanji/除.md) carries removal or exclusion, and く completes the native verb のぞく.
24: The same basic idea works for a physical object and for a member left out of a stated group.
25: 
26: ## Synonyms and antonyms
27: 
28: 取り除く (とりのぞく) also means taking something away.
29: [含む](含む.md) (ふくむ), "include; contain," provides the useful contrast for sets:
30: 日曜日を含む (にちようびをふくむ) includes Sunday, while 日曜日を除く excludes it.
31: 
32: ## Distinctive meaning
33: 
34: An exception does not imply destruction or rejection of the thing itself.
35: In a schedule, Xを除く changes which days the statement applies to. Check the noun before を carefully:
36: that is the exception, not the permitted group.
37:

12: # 外す (はずす) - remove; unfasten
13: 
14: ## Meaning
15: 
16: 外す means to remove, detach, or unfasten something. It is a transitive godan verb: 外します, 外した, 外さない. Use を for the thing removed.
17: 
18: - 眼鏡を外して、本を置きました。 (めがねをはずして、ほんをおきました。) - I took off my glasses and put down the book.
19: - シャツのボタンを一つ外しました。 (シャツのボタンをひとつはずしました。) - I undid one button on my shirt.
20: 
21: The button example means unfastening it in this context, not necessarily cutting it off the shirt.
22: 
23: ## How the kanji combine
24: 
25: [外](../kanji/外.md) contributes the idea of being out of an attached or expected position. In this verb it is read はず before す. Do not substitute the noun reading そと into the verb.
26: 
27: ## Synonyms and antonyms
28: 
29: 外れる (はずれる) is the intransitive partner: ボタンが外れた, "the button came undone." [脱ぐ](脱ぐ.md) (ぬぐ) is used for taking off clothing, while [取る](取る.md) (とる) has broader taking and removing uses.
30: 
31: ## Distinctive meaning
32: 
33: 外す also appears in 席を外す (せきをはずす), "step away from one's seat; be temporarily away," and 的を外す (まとをはずす), "miss the target." Neither requires removing a physical component. The object identifies the intended sense, so "remove" is a starting gloss rather than a translation that fits every construction.
34:

12: # 省く (はぶく) - omit; cut down on
13: 
14: ## Meaning
15: 
16: 省く means to omit or leave something out, or to save effort or expense by
17: cutting it down. It is a transitive godan verb: mark what is omitted or saved
18: with を.
19: 
20: - 時間がないので、詳しい説明は省きます。 (じかんがないので、くわしいせつめいははぶきます。) - Since there is no time, I will omit the detailed explanation.
21: - この道具を使うと、手間を省けます。 (このどうぐをつかうと、てまをはぶけます。) - Using this tool saves effort.
22: 
23: 省きます (はぶきます) is polite nonpast; 省いて (はぶいて) is the て-form.
24: 省ける (はぶける) is the potential form, "can omit/save."
25: 
26: ## How the kanji combine
27: 
28: [省](../kanji/省.md) contributes omitting or economizing in this word. The native verb is
29: はぶく, not the on reading ショウ used in some compounds. The final く
30: changes with conjugation.
31: 
32: ## Synonyms and antonyms
33: 
34: [除く](除く.md) (のぞく) overlaps in excluding or removing.
35: 省略 (しょうりゃく) means omission or abbreviation and overlaps when leaving
36: part of an explanation out. Adding information is a contextual opposite,
37: not the meaning of one fixed antonym.
38: 
39: ## Distinctive meaning
40: 
41: 省く often concerns reducing what a process requires, as in 手間を省く.
42: It does not automatically mean careless omission: the result may be an
43: efficient procedure. Conversely, omitting something does not prove that
44: it was unimportant; the surrounding explanation supplies the reason.
45:

 13: 
 14: ## Meaning
 15: 
 16: 省く means to omit or leave something out, or to save effort or expense by
 17: cutting it down. It is a transitive godan verb: mark what is omitted or saved
 18: with を.
 19: 
 20: - 時間がないので、詳しい説明は省きます。 (じかんがないので、くわしいせつめいははぶきます。) - Since there is no time, I will omit the detailed explanation.
 21: - この道具を使うと、手間を省けます。 (このどうぐをつかうと、てまをはぶけます。) - Using this tool saves effort.
 22: 
 23: 省きます (はぶきます) is polite nonpast; 省いて (はぶいて) is the て-form.
 24: 省ける (はぶける) is the potential form, "can omit/save."
 25: 
 26: ## How the kanji combine
 27: 
 28: [省](../kanji/省.md) contributes omitting or economizing in this word. The native verb is
 29: はぶく, not the on reading ショウ used in some compounds. The final く
 30: changes with conjugation.
 31: 
 32: ## Synonyms and antonyms
 33: 
 34: [除く](除く.md) (のぞく) overlaps in excluding or removing.
 35: 省略 (しょうりゃく) means omission or abbreviation and overlaps when leaving
 36: part of an explanation out. Adding information is a contextual opposite,
 37: not the meaning of one fixed antonym.
 38: 
 39: ## Distinctive meaning
 40: 
 41: 省く often concerns reducing what a process requires, as in 手間を省く.
 42: It does not automatically mean careless omission: the result may be an
 43: efficient procedure. Conversely, omitting something does not prove that
